modules.title: Linked certifications
modules.need: Certified content is outside content and must be linked and tracked
modules.roles: req All by role; managers' certificates included
modules.unlock: H (enrollment at hire; certifications run on their own clock)
modules.approach: Linked, never written (D17): harassment prevention, workplace safety, food handler, alcohol service (TABC Safe Harbor requires certification within a window and a written house policy, VP), first aid and CPR, manager-level certificates. tool.compliance.*
modules.afterThis: After this, a person holds every certificate their role requires, uploaded and verified, and can say which certificate covers which part of their work and when it renews.
teaches: Which outside certificates each role needs and where each comes from: harassment prevention and workplace safety from Trainual's add-on library; food handler, Texas alcohol seller-server (TABC), first aid and CPR, and the food protection manager certificate from outside providers (D17, D27). Role map is tool.compliance.role_map

TABC Safe Harbor in plain terms: the employer's defense requires every person who sells or serves alcohol, and their manager, certified within the window the law sets, plus written house policies each person has read and signed (Texas Alcoholic Beverage Code 106.14; TABC certification FAQs). The house policy is founder.responsible_service_policy
That a certificate is the legal floor the house builds on, not the house's standard; the house craft on top lives in SAF-001, SAF-009, SAF-011 and SAF-003
How to enroll, upload a certificate, and see a renewal coming: tool.compliance.enrollment, tool.compliance.upload, workflow.certificate_renewal
Manager-level certificates and who must hold them (food protection manager, TABC for the immediate manager of servers): tool.compliance.manager_certificates
modules.leaves: No certified content is written or re-taught here (D17); the providers teach it. The house's craft on top: allergy taking (SAF-001), alcohol service decisions (SAF-009), food safety behavior (SAF-011), cryogenic equipment procedure (SAF-003), the first minute of an emergency (SAF-006).
modules.proven: The certificate is uploaded and an Admin verifies it; a lapsed certificate removes the person from the work it covers until renewed. No conversation or practical.
modules.waitsOn: The compliance tool and provider choices (tool.compliance.*), the house alcohol policy for Safe Harbor (founder.responsible_service_policy), and provider costs as fact.* bindings.
modules.recommendation: keep: the tracking row every role passes through at hire; it holds no content of its own.

modules.title: Taking an allergy at the table, and needs that are not allergies
modules.need: Allergy routing depends on a server judging severity; a religious or ethical restriction is treated as a preference, or a substitution is promised the kitchen cannot make
modules.roles: req All customer-facing W; BOH chain side chef-gated; host arrival bank
modules.approach: Branching scenario around the moment of doubt; facts in the job aid; the non-allergy bank (was SAF-008) on the same routing frame; beverage allergen cases. Ties to KIT-003. First in the elicitation queue
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can take a customer's allergy or dietary need, confirm it back in the customer's words, route it to the kitchen without judging its severity, and say only what the kitchen has confirmed it can do.
teaches: The nine major food allergens US law recognizes (milk, egg, fish, crustacean shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, soybeans, sesame) and that a customer's allergy to anything else is routed the same way (FALCPA 2004; FASTER Act 2021, FDA)

The house rule: a stated allergy is never judged for severity, size, or sincerity by the server; it is taken, read back, and routed every time, including when it arrives mid-meal or from the reservation note (module need; SVC-058, SVC-017 route here)

Needs that are not allergies (religious, ethical, medical diets, intolerances) are taken with the same care and routed on the same frame, never treated as a preference to be bargained with (was SAF-008)

Never promising a substitution or a 'safe' dish before the kitchen confirms; what the floor may say, and what it hands to the kitchen. The allergen matrix is chef.allergen_matrix; the routing path is workflow.allergy_routing; the record is tool.pos.allergen_flag
Beverage allergens and hidden sources at the bar (for example nut, dairy, egg, or sesame in a drink component): people.head_of_beverage and chef.allergen_matrix

The signs that a reaction is starting (hives, swelling of lips or throat, trouble breathing, vomiting, faintness) as a cue to hand off to SAF-006 at once, not to treat (Red Cross, anaphylaxis guidance)
modules.leaves: The certified food handler and allergen awareness content (SAF-002). Cross-contact in prep and at the pass (SAF-013, chef-gated). Getting the modified plate to the right seat (SAF-004). Responding to a reaction (SAF-006, with first aid linked). The kitchen's side of the handoff (KIT-003).
modules.proven: A short spoken check of the routing and the do-not-say lines at T0, then a branching scenario and a role-play at T1; the allergy element is non-compensatory at G1 to G3 and passes in every attempt (D11). Never challenged away (D39).
modules.waitsOn: The chef's allergen matrix (chef.allergen_matrix) and the head of beverage for the drink cases; the routing workflow (workflow.allergy_routing) and the POS flag are bindings. The durable frame can be drafted now.
modules.recommendation: keep: the hard prerequisite before any customer contact.

modules.title: Delivering a modified plate
modules.need: An allergy-modified plate reaches the wrong seat or leaves without a check
modules.approach: Branching scenario around the moment of doubt at the table; facts in the job aid
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can identify a modified plate, confirm it against the order before it leaves the pass, set it at the right seat with a spoken check to the customer, and stop the plate when anything does not match.
teaches: How a modified plate is marked and recognized at the pass, and that an unmarked or uncertain plate does not leave: chef.allergen_marking
The check before the plate moves (seat, allergy, modification) as a closed loop with expo, the same call and check-back as SVC-013 (TeamSTEPPS check-back, AHRQ): workflow.allergy_delivery
Setting the plate at the right seat first, and confirming the modification to the customer at set-down in the house's words without alarming the table
The stop rule: any doubt (wrong seat, missing mark, a new allergy mentioned at the table, a garnish or sauce that does not match) sends the plate back, and who to tell
What happens to a plate that went wrong, and that it is reported, not hidden (ties to SAF-011)
modules.leaves: Taking and routing the allergy (SAF-001). Cross-contact in prep and plating (SAF-013, chef-gated). Carry technique (SVC-003). Seat numbering (SVC-019). Responding to a reaction (SAF-006).
modules.proven: A banked drill run at the pass and table with planted errors, then observation on the angel shift; the check is non-compensatory at G1 to G3 and passes in every attempt (D11).
modules.waitsOn: The chef's marking system (chef.allergen_marking) and the delivery workflow (workflow.allergy_delivery); position numbering (workflow.position_numbering) for the seat check.
modules.recommendation: keep: a separate job for runners and back waiters that SAF-001 does not drill, and the second safety element at G2.

modules.title: Noticing someone in trouble
modules.need: People notice a customer or teammate in distress (a reaction, intoxication, a fall, harassment) and assume someone else has it
modules.approach: Cue clips then a named move: name one person, aloud. Diffusion of responsibility (Darley and Latané 1968, VS). Medical content linked; workflow.emergency.*
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can spot the early signs that a customer or teammate is in distress and make the first move themselves: naming one specific person aloud to act, rather than assuming someone else has it.
teaches: Diffusion of responsibility: why a crowded room makes each person less likely to act, and the counter-move of naming one person aloud (Darley and Latané 1968)
The cues worth noticing on a floor: a reaction starting, a fall or faintness, choking, rising intoxication, a customer or teammate being harassed or cornered

Where each cue routes: a reaction or medical event to SAF-006; intoxication to SAF-009 and the lead; harassment to the house conduct policy and the floor manager (founder.conduct_policy, workflow.escalation)
The authority line on the floor: the server owns the table, the floor manager owns the room, and escalation triggers are set before service (BG 15 'Floor authority')
modules.leaves: Medical response and bystander intervention as certified content (first aid and CPR, harassment prevention, both linked through SAF-002). The emergency sequence itself (SAF-006). Slowing alcohol service (SAF-009).
modules.proven: A cue-clip check: the person names what they saw and the one move they make; a simulation item at G2.
modules.waitsOn: The emergency plan (workflow.emergency_plan) and escalation routing (workflow.escalation); the conduct policy for customers who cross a line (D50, founder policy).
modules.recommendation: merge into SAF-006: same cohort, same timing, and the same named move; noticing is the opening beat of the first minute, kept as SAF-006's cue bank.

modules.title: The first minute of an emergency
modules.need: In fire, medical, choking, allergic-reaction or evacuation events, people freeze, crowd, or wait for a manager
modules.approach: Drilled rehearsal on site. Durable part: who calls, who holds the room, the customer's dignity. First aid and CPR linked (D17). Ties to SAF-001
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can act in the first minute of a fire, medical, choking, allergic-reaction, or evacuation event at Sŏn: call for help or assign the call by name, get the right equipment, hold the room, and protect the customer's dignity, without waiting for a manager.
teaches: The first-minute roles: one person calls emergency services, one person brings equipment, one person holds the room and keeps space; assigned by name, aloud (Darley and Latané 1968; recognized first aid sequence: check, call, care, American Red Cross)

Anaphylaxis specifically: a customer's own epinephrine is used as directed and emergency services are called even if symptoms ease, because they can return (American Red Cross); who may assist is set by policy and the linked first aid course

The house's emergency plan: who calls, where the equipment is (first aid kit, fire extinguishers, the fireplace and live-fire shutoffs, exits), the evacuation route and meeting point: workflow.emergency_plan, workflow.emergency.equipment_locations
Holding the room: keeping other customers calm and informed, clearing a path for responders, screening the affected customer from view, and what is never said to the table
After the minute: handing over to responders and to the floor manager, and what is recorded: workflow.incident_report
Cue bank (from SAF-005): spotting the start of an emergency and naming one person aloud
modules.leaves: First aid, CPR, and fire extinguisher technique as certified content (linked, SAF-002, D17). Allergy taking (SAF-001). Kitchen fire and chemical response at the station (SAF-012, chef-gated). Facility systems and their maintenance.
modules.proven: An on-site drill per scenario type, run in the real room; the person's role in the first minute passes in every attempt (D11); rechecked on the standing recheck cadence (workflow.recheck_cadence).
modules.waitsOn: The house emergency plan and equipment locations (workflow.emergency_plan, workflow.emergency.*), which wait on the building; the first aid and CPR provider (tool.compliance.first_aid).
modules.recommendation: keep: absorbs SAF-005 as its cue bank.

modules.title: Moving safely in a shared space
modules.need: People move through shared floor and kitchen space without the house calls: collisions, burns, cuts
modules.approach: Drilled rehearsal. Charnas, *Work Clean*, call and callback (VS); closed-loop communication from trauma teams (Härgestam 2013, VS). Calls chef-gated (chef.call_language). Shares KIT-016
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can move through the floor, the bar, and the kitchen threshold using the house calls and callbacks, carry hot, sharp, or heavy items safely, and stop a collision before it happens.
teaches: Call and callback as a closed loop: a call is not complete until it is answered (Charnas, Work Clean; closed-loop communication in trauma teams, Härgestam 2013)
The house movement calls (behind, corner, hot, sharp, door) and their exact words: chef.call_language for the kitchen side, workflow.floor_calls for the floor
Hazard carries: hot plates and pans, knives and broken glass, trays and heavy loads, liquids near the fireplace and live fire, with the body mechanics of a safe lift
Traffic rules for the shared spaces: right of way, blind corners, the service threshold, wet floors and spills: workflow.traffic_rules, layout bound to the built room
modules.leaves: Workplace safety and injury reporting as certified content (Trainual add-on, SAF-002). Kitchen station safety, chemicals and equipment (SAF-012, KIT-016, chef-gated). Carry technique as craft (SVC-003). Communication calls about orders and allergies (SVC-013).
modules.proven: A banked movement drill on site at tempo with the calls; observed again on the angel shift.
modules.waitsOn: The chef's call language (chef.call_language) and the built floor plan (workflow.traffic_rules).
modules.recommendation: keep: the trunk version that KIT-016 deepens for the kitchen; draft them as one family with a kitchen bank.

modules.title: Food safety culture: the floor nobody watches
modules.need: Safety is treated as the certificate, not as behavior when unobserved or rushed
modules.gate: G1 item; NC in every kitchen gate
modules.approach: Short cases on speaking up about a hazard across levels; the certificate itself is linked (SAF-002). FDA's food safety culture definition as the frame (VP). Sensor logging is tool.food_safety.logging
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can explain why food safety is what people do when nobody is watching or the night is rushed, spot a hazard on the floor or the bar, and raise it to anyone, at any level, at the moment it happens.
teaches: Food safety culture as behavior, not a certificate: the shared values, beliefs, and norms that shape how people think and act on food safety (FDA, New Era of Smarter Food Safety)
Speaking up about a hazard across levels: how to say it to a lead or a founder in one line, and the house rule that stopping a hazard is never penalized (ties to the non-negotiables, BG 01)

The floor and bar hazards that slip under pressure: hand washing and glove use, ice handling, cutting boards and garnishes, temperature-sensitive items left out, dropped items: house specifics chef.* and workflow.*
What sensor logging records and that the person still owns the check: tool.food_safety.logging (WP, the defensive stack)
Reporting an error or near miss without hiding it, and what happens next: workflow.food_safety_report
modules.leaves: Food handler and manager certificate content: time and temperature rules, sanitation, illness exclusion (SAF-002). Allergen cross-contact in production (SAF-013). Kitchen station specifics (chef.*, KIT rows). Chemicals (SAF-012).
modules.proven: A short conversation on one case at G1; in every kitchen gate the food safety element is non-compensatory and passes in every attempt (D11).
modules.waitsOn: The chef for kitchen specifics (chef.*); the sensor logging tool (tool.food_safety.logging) for that one point. The durable frame can be drafted now.
modules.recommendation: keep: the only module that teaches behavior on top of the certificate.

modules.title: Slowing or stopping alcohol service with dignity
modules.need: Certification covers the law, not the house's craft: novices ignore the signs, confront publicly, or avoid the call
modules.roles: req BT W (before G3); FS H MD leads W
modules.gate: NC element at the bar practical
modules.approach: Role-play with a stop rule and TBRI. Johnstone: lower your own status so the customer keeps face (VS); de-escalation (LO). The written house policy must exist first (TABC Safe Harbor, VP)
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can read the signs that a customer has had enough, slow or stop service privately with a lead's backing, and keep the customer's dignity, following the written house policy.
teaches: The written house responsible-service policy and how it extends the TABC certificate; the policy must exist before this module can be drafted (Texas Alcoholic Beverage Code 106.14; founder.responsible_service_policy)
Reading the signs across a meal: pace, behavior, coordination and speech, and what the customer has eaten, kept in a running read rather than a single moment
Slowing before stopping: pacing, water and food, the non-alcoholic offer, and when a lead is brought in: workflow.alcohol_escalation
Stopping without public confrontation: lowering one's own status so the customer keeps face (Johnstone, Impro), de-escalation language, and never doing it alone
Getting the customer home safely, and what is recorded afterward: workflow.safe_ride, workflow.incident_report
modules.leaves: The law, intoxication signs as certified content, and ID checking (TABC seller-server, linked through SAF-002). Customers who cross a line in other ways (the house policy for that, D50). Medical emergencies (SAF-006).
modules.proven: A role-play with a stop rule, debrief, and a private first pass; the responsible-service element is non-compensatory at the bar practical and passes in every attempt (D11).
modules.waitsOn: The written responsible-service policy from Brandon (founder.responsible_service_policy; D50). TABC certification (SAF-002) before the module opens.
modules.recommendation: keep: the certificate covers the law, not the house's craft of the call.

modules.title: Cryogenic and pressure equipment in beverage prep
modules.need: Liquid nitrogen and pressurized holding (WP p.4) are handled without trained procedure
modules.approach: Linked supplier and standards training (tool.compliance.cryogen); house procedure bound
modules.afterThis: After this, a preparer can handle, dispense, and store liquid nitrogen and work the pressurized holding system following the house procedure, name each hazard, and stop and report when something is wrong.
teaches: The hazards of liquid nitrogen: cold burns and frostbite on contact, oxygen displacement and asphyxiation in poorly ventilated spaces, and pressure build-up in sealed containers (FDA 2018 advisory on liquid nitrogen in food; Poison Control)
That no product reaches a customer while liquid nitrogen is still present; the batch is chilled in the back and held, not served smoking (WP p.4; FDA 2018 advisory)

Protective equipment, the right vessels, transfer and storage, ventilation, and the oxygen monitor if one is installed: supplier training and house procedure, tool.compliance.cryogen and workflow.cryogen_procedure
The pressurized, oxygen-free holding system: compressed gas cylinders, connections, pressure checks, and the safe release before service work: supplier procedure, workflow.pressure_holding
What to do on a spill, a leak, a cold burn, or someone feeling faint near the storage area, routed to SAF-006
modules.leaves: The supplier's and the standards body's certified handling training (linked, tool.compliance.cryogen). The espresso and batch method itself (BEV-018, founder and chef). Kitchen chemicals and equipment (SAF-012).
modules.proven: A supervised practical on the actual equipment with the procedure steps; every safety step passes in every attempt (D11); rechecked on a set cadence (workflow.recheck_cadence).
modules.waitsOn: The equipment and its supplier (tool.compliance.cryogen), the head of beverage (people.head_of_beverage), and the written house procedure.
modules.recommendation: keep: a real hazard named in the white paper, and the prerequisite for BEV-018.

modules.title: Allergen and food-safety steward
modules.need: Allergy knowledge lives only in the kitchen, and nobody on the floor holds the whole chain
modules.approach: The house's own practice on top of a linked credential; teaches the chain at pre-shift. The safety Student star
modules.afterThis: After this, a person can explain the whole allergy chain from the reservation note to the plate at the seat, spot where it can break, and teach it at pre-shift.
teaches: The whole chain end to end: the reservation note, the take at the table, the kitchen ticket, cross-contact control, the marked plate, the delivery check (SAF-001, SAF-013, SAF-004; chef.allergen_matrix)
Where the chain breaks under pressure: handoffs between shifts and dayparts, menu changes, new hires, substitutions (SVC-017)
Teaching the chain at pre-shift in a short form, and checking a teammate's understanding without testing them in front of others (LEA teaching rows)
Keeping the house current: what changes the allergen information on a menu change and who updates it: workflow.allergen_update
The advanced credential's content as the base the house practice sits on (for example a certified allergen or food protection manager course, linked, D17)
modules.leaves: The certified allergen and food protection content (linked advanced credential through SAF-002). Taking and delivering an allergy (SAF-001, SAF-004). Production cross-contact (SAF-013, chef-gated).
modules.proven: The linked credential uploaded, plus a conversation in which the person walks the chain and teaches it once at pre-shift under observation.
modules.waitsOn: The chef's allergen matrix and the allergy routing and delivery workflows (chef.allergen_matrix, workflow.allergy_routing, workflow.allergy_delivery); the choice of advanced credential (tool.compliance.allergen_credential).
modules.recommendation: keep: an elective star that gives the floor someone who holds the whole chain; content beyond SAF-001 is only the teaching and the chain view.
